entry.title: Social Summary: November 25, 2026
entry.summary: Accessibility & community building (lead item): The clear winner is the official @NousResearch reply to @AviSchiffmann noting that 'scrappy users' are building wonderful things with free and heavily discounted models — the week's top post by far (294 likes, ~7.9k views) and an on-mission message that cheap, broad model access is fueling grassroots projects across the Hermes ecosystem; it doubles as a cultural statement that fits the newsletter's open-weights ethos. Official account engagement (short replies): Three low-content replies round out the section — a playful confirmation to @kerwinv101 ('Yes it's his hair') in a thread tagging @NVIDIAAI (18 likes), an affirming 'Always' to @bippolaroid (8 likes, ~1.2k views), and a one-word 'Sick' reacting to a @Teknium-adjacent demo (@__RobertG__ thread, 1 like, 427 views); these are tie-broken by residual engagement, with the Teknium nod flagged as a possible early signal of in-house work worth watching in future issues. Sentiment: Community tone is positive, and the official account reads as approachable, quick to reply, and community-first; engagement clusters around the substantive accessibility statement rather than the banter, so the three replies carry personality and brand-voice value more than standalone news value — worth including mainly to convey the team's responsive, scrappy culture.

entry.title: Social Summary: November 24, 2026
entry.summary:
Oh-My-Hermes Desktop & Ecosystem Launch: The standout community story is @rlaope's launch of Oh-My-Hermes (OMHER Desktop), an open-source desktop app built on Hermes Agent that has surged past 6k GitHub stars — 'a face for every bot' featuring a GrokBot companion, with repo and download links shared in-thread. Ecosystem momentum extends across the batch: day-one oh-my-hermes provider support for the newly announced GLM 5.4 (not yet in our model-tracking reference, suggesting a fresh same-week release), a 6k-star Hermes-Agent Plugin milestone thank-you, free Hermes Agent motion reels, and a deep three-day engineering retrospective running Oh-My-Hermes on 3x RTX 6000 Pro — covering SGLang DSA fixes, Triton/FlashInfer kernels, AWQ/GPTQ quantization, a path-traversal security fix, and vLLM KV-cache verification.

Enterprise Strategy & Roadmap: @Teknium delivered the batch's most substantive strategic statement, correcting skepticism in the @pabis_eu thread: Hermes enterprise plans existed from day one, with an enterprise team in place since April and named design partners. Supporting replies point users to enterprise@nousresearch.com, welcome collaborations with NVIDIA and Microsoft, disclose the Mozilla Foundation as an investor alongside the Linux Foundation, cite 'hundreds of NDAs' including Microsoft, and deny a rumored Qwen-finetune commission. @Teknium also teased a bots marketplace coming to the Hermes Market. Sentiment here is engaged but contentious — skeptics press on partnership purity, and Teknium mixes real disclosure with banter.

Frontier Model Discounts: The highest-reach posts of the batch: an official Nous Research announcement of 20% off the latest Anthropic and OpenAI models for one week (~200k views, 486 likes), amplified by @Teknium's 'Big discounts on Claude and GPT' (7.5k views) — clear community enthusiasm for cheaper frontier access via Nous.

Multi-Agent Delegation: @rlaope announced that Hermes Agent can now hand coding work to agents users already pay for — beyond Codex, Claude Code, and pi, it adds built-in support for Devin, Gemini CLI, Qwen and more, with git-verified results, worktree isolation, and session continuity; the desktop app adds sub-agent routing. Well received as a practical orchestration upgrade.

Industry Commentary: @rlaope flags OpenAI chief scientist Jakub Pachocki publishing internal pretraining loss numbers (log-perplexity gains on held-out code) as a rare transparency move, offers a wry take on Anthropic's claimed proof of the Riemann Hypothesis ('proven true, but not understood by people'), and names GPT 6.2 as the model they trust most at the implementation level across their multi-model workflow.

Community Sentiment: Official hype ('We're so back') pulled 4k+ likes / 52k views, @Teknium's 'Truly part of the Hermes Agent gang now' resonated at 10k+ views / 208 likes, and Nous publicly vouched that a viral Hermes clip is 'not edited'. Overall: a high-momentum week in which open-source ecosystem growth (OMHER), enterprise credibility, and discount-driven reach reinforce each other.

entry.title:
3-day kernel grinding retrospective with 3x RTX 6000 Pro and Oh-My-Hermes
- Fixed SGLang ignoring t...
entry.summary: rlaope publishing a detailed three-day retrospective of kernel and inference-stack fixes using 3x RTX 6000 Pro and Oh-My-Hermes, including SGLang DSA prefill config fixes on SM120, Qwen3.6 AWQ load crash fix, a custom Marlin inverse transform with bit-exact verification across 44 test cases (referencing PR #52330), Qwen3-Coder tool-call constraint fixes, a blocked path traversal on /start_profile (#52351), Triton build fixes, FlashInfer SM120 JIT race condition fix, and verification of a vLLM KV-cache PR halving memory use.

entry.title: OpenAI published its internal pretraining loss numbers, the kind of thing labs usually keep to thems...
entry.summary: rlaope summarizes OpenAI chief scientist Jakub Pachocki publishing internal pretraining loss numbers: log-perplexity on a held-out code set improving from about 0.99 (GPT-3.5) to 0.91 (GPT-4), around 0.76 producing groundbreaking math results, with the next capability jump expected in the 0.68-0.70 range, and a call for common cross-lab capability limits measured this way.
